Truant

TROO-unt · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Truant is a person, especially a student, who is absent without permission, particularly from school.

The attendance officer spent every Tuesday tracking down truants around the neighborhood.

Worked Example

As a boy, he was a notorious truant, spending more afternoons at the river than in the classroom.

He wasn't occasionally late -- he was habitually and intentionally absent without permission, which is exactly a truant.

How Truant Sits Among Its Neighbors

absentee

absentee: a person who is not present when expected

dodger: someone who avoids an obligation or duty

Antonyms

attendee

attendee: a person who is present at an event or place

How Strong Is It? — latecomer → truant → dropout

latecomer vs. truant

latecomer vs. truant: A latecomer simply arrives after the start; a truant is absent entirely, and without permission.

dropout vs. truant

dropout vs. truant: A truant still skips school occasionally, planning to return; a dropout has left school entirely and does not intend to come back.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Truant comes from Old French truant, 'beggar, vagabond,' itself likely from an older Celtic word for someone impoverished or homeless.

Where it comes from

Where it comes from: Truant originally had nothing to do with school: in Old French it meant a beggar or vagabond, likely from an even older Celtic word for someone poor and homeless. Only later did English narrow the idea of an idle wanderer down to a student who wanders off instead of showing up to class.

Word Building

Word Choice

Truant is most often used as a noun for the student themselves, though it can also function as an adjective ("truant behavior").
